title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 22 October 2026 (week 43) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: The report is based on data up to week 42 of 2026 between 12 October and 18 October 2026. The publication date is 22 October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The report covers England, focusing on the population aged 75 years and over, and those under 75 years with a weakened immune system.
analysis.event: The report summarizes the surveillance data for SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), influenza, and other seasonal respiratory viruses in England during week 42 of 2026. It notes that SARS-CoV-2 activity showed mixed trends and was circulating at low levels, with ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness increasing slightly and confirmed ARI incidents increasing compared with the previous week.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of 20 October 2026, there were 1,915 COVID-19 cases identified in hospital settings in week 42, remaining stable compared with 2,007 cases in the previous week. The rolling 7-day positivity rate for SARS-CoV-2 in hospital settings was 8.9% up to Sunday 18 October 2026, with positivity rates highest among those aged 85 years and over at 13.4%.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report indicates that there were issues with unavailable or incomplete influenza vaccination data in weeks 41 and 42, which were corrected for week 43. The data quality report outlines changes in testing policy during 2022 to 2023, and testing policy and practice may change over time, impacting positivity rates. Comparisons over time should be interpreted with caution.

analysis.brief_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 22 October 2026 (week 43) provides an overview of respiratory virus activity in England. It notes that SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) activity showed mixed trends, with low circulation levels and a slight increase in emergency department (ED) attendances for COVID-19-like illness. The number of confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents increased compared to the previous week, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 8.9% in hospital settings. Positivity rates were highest among those aged 85 years and over, at 13.4%. The report highlights that influenza activity remained stable, with ED attendances for influenza-like illness increasing slightly. Vaccine uptake data for the 2026 to 2027 season showed lower rates among certain groups, such as those aged 65 and over, and those in clinical risk groups, but higher uptake among pregnant women. The report also mentions that data quality issues affected the availability of influenza vaccination data in weeks 41 and 42, which were corrected for week 43. Testing policy changes over time may influence positivity rates, and comparisons should be made cautiously. The report is based on data up to week 42, ending on 18 October 2026.
